zh.sourceText: 某媒体调查显示，78% 的受访者支持在市中心修建新的高架桥。报道称，市民普遍支持该项目，所以高架桥应该尽快开工。【gap:gap1】调查由市交通局出资，只访问了 200 名经常开车的受访者，其中多数住在桥址附近。市政府的新闻稿随即转引了这一数据，称『民心所向，当尽快动工』。环保组织则提醒，高架桥可能加剧沿线区域的空气污染。某地产商趁势宣传：『桥通了，房价起飞！』

textRefs.gap1_correct: 调查由市交通局出资，只访问了 200 名经常开车、多数住在桥址附近的受访者——样本与出资方都偏向支持方，根本不能代表全体市民

gap1: 调查由市交通局出资，只访问了 200 名经常开车、多数住在桥址附近的受访者——样本与出资方都偏向支持方，根本不能代表全体市民
高架桥的建设工期预计为三年，建成后能分流两成车流
市政府此前多次召开过公开听证会，程序并无缺失

hints: 先扫描结论与理由：『市民普遍支持』这个前提来自哪里？
正文里藏着几处关于调查的细节，把它们串起来看
调查是谁出钱的？受访者是怎么被选中的？
zh.explanation: 结论是「高架桥应该尽快开工」，理由是『78% 受访者支持』。但把正文里的碎片拼起来：调查由交通局出资、只访问了 200 名开车族、多数还住在桥址附近——样本和出资方都偏向支持方，根本代表不了全体市民；市政府转引、地产商炒作更是各怀目的。这就是「遗漏信息」的陷阱：看到『XX% 的人支持』，先问样本是谁、怎么选的、谁出的钱。

en.sourceText: A media survey reports that 78% of respondents support building a new viaduct downtown. The report claims residents broadly support the project, so construction should start soon.【gap:gap1】The survey was funded by the city's transport bureau and covered only 200 respondents who drive regularly, most of them living near the proposed site. The city government's press release promptly cited the figure, declaring 'the people want it — work should begin without delay'. Environmental groups warn that a viaduct could worsen air pollution along the corridor. A real-estate developer is cashing in: 'Bridge opens, property prices take off!'

textRefs.gap1_correct: The survey was funded by the transport bureau and covered only 200 regular drivers, most living near the proposed site — both the sample and the funder lean toward supporters, so it cannot represent all residents

gap1: The survey was funded by the transport bureau and covered only 200 regular drivers, most living near the proposed site — both the sample and the funder lean toward supporters, so it cannot represent all residents
The viaduct is expected to take three years to build and will divert one fifth of the traffic
The city has held several public hearings before, so the procedure is complete

hints: Scan for the conclusion and the reason: where does the premise of 'broad support' come from?
Several details about the survey are scattered in the text — connect them
Who funded the survey? How were the respondents chosen?
en.explanation: The conclusion is 'construction should start soon', supported by '78% of respondents support it'. But piece the fragments together: the survey was funded by the transport bureau, covered only 200 regular drivers, most living near the site — both sample and funder lean toward supporters, so it represents no one but supporters; the city citing the figure and the developer hyping it each have their own agenda. That is the trap of omitted information: whenever you see 'X% of people support', ask who was sampled, how they were chosen, and who paid.
